title: SSVEP MAMEM 3 dataset
description: This dataset comprises 14-channel EEG recordings from 11 healthy subjects performing steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) tasks with five flickering frequencies (6.66–12.00 Hz). The dataset supports comparative evaluation of signal processing algorithms for SSVEP-based brain-computer interfaces, including filtering, artifact removal, feature extraction, and classification methods. Preprocessed data and comprehensive documentation enable reproducible benchmarking of BCI algorithms.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using an EGI 300 Geodesic EEG System at 128 Hz sampling rate from 14 scalp electrodes in 10-20 montage (AF3, AF4, F3, F4, F7, F8, FC5, FC6, O1, O2, P7, P8, T7, T8). Subjects attended to a violet flickering box presented on a 22-inch LCD monitor (60 Hz refresh rate) at one of five frequencies per trial. Each 5-second trial was followed by 5 seconds of rest. Data were preprocessed with bandpass filtering (5–48 Hz), 50 Hz notch filtering, and artifact removal using AMUSE and ICA. Common Average Reference was applied for re-referencing. Comparative evaluation of state-of-the-art algorithms was performed using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, examining filtering methods (IIR, FIR), artifact removal techniques (AMUSE, ICA), feature extraction methods (Periodogram, Welch, Goertzel, Yule-AR, STFT, DWT), feature selection (Shannon entropy, PCA, ICA), and classification algorithms (LDA, SVM, kNN, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, CCA, ELM, Decision Trees).
